name: default
finder_guidance: Report concrete vulnerabilities, not hardening suggestions or missing best practices.

specialists.name: untrusted-deserialization
specialists.focus: Attacker-influenced bytes, or a request-selected file or name, reaching a deserializer that can instantiate objects or run code.
specialists.guidance: Sources: request parameters, form and JSON fields, uploads, cookies, headers, tokens or assertions from external identity providers, stored user data, and names or paths that select which file gets loaded. Sinks: Python pickle/cPickle/dill/joblib.load(s), torch.load without weights_only=True, yaml.load without a safe loader; Java ObjectInputStream.readObject and deserialization inside token, state, or nonce decoders; PHP unserialize; Ruby Marshal.load and YAML.load; .NET BinaryFormatter and NetDataContractSerializer; JSON with polymorphic or default typing enabled. Defenses to check: safe loader or weights_only, class allow-lists, signature or HMAC verification before decoding, authenticated encryption, and a fixed trusted location writable only by operators. Report when the diff adds or keeps such a sink and the bytes, or the selected file, can come from a user or external party. Do not report a fixed file that only trusted operators can write. When a user-selected name is joined into a directory path, report only if it can escape the directory or allowed names are not enforced server-side.
